name: es20-framebuffer-objects
title: Framebuffer objects: render to texture, renderbuffers, completeness
summary: Texture and renderbuffer attachments (RGBA8, DEPTH_COMPONENT16/24, STENCIL_INDEX8, DEPTH24_STENCIL8 via DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT, a mip level, a depth texture) proven by pixel comparison against CPU models, depth- and stencil-tested draws that only work if the attachment exists, framebuffer completeness including the failures ES 3.0 defines, INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION, attachment/renderbuffer queries and the object lifecycle.
spec: ES 3.0 §4.4.1 Binding and Managing Framebuffer Objects

ES 3.0 §4.4.2 Attaching Images to Framebuffer Objects (§4.4.2.1 Renderbuffer Objects, §4.4.2.2 Required Renderbuffer Formats, §4.4.2.3 Attaching Renderbuffer Images, §4.4.2.4 Attaching Texture Images)
ES 3.0 §4.4.3 Feedback Loops Between Textures and the Framebuffer (documented, deliberately not rendered)
ES 3.0 §4.4.4 Framebuffer Completeness (§4.4.4.1 attachment completeness, §4.4.4.2 whole framebuffer completeness, §4.4.4.4 effects of incompleteness on framebuffer operations)
ES 3.0 §4.1.4 Stencil Test, §4.1.5 Depth Buffer Test, §4.2.2 Fine Control of Buffer Updates, §4.2.3 Clearing the Buffers
ES 3.0 §4.3.3 Copying Pixels (glBlitFramebuffer, only used to show renderbuffers on the screen)
ES 3.0 §3.8.3 Texture Image Specification (Tables 3.13 and 3.14: color-/depth-renderable formats), §3.8.13 Texture Completeness
ES 3.0 §6.1.13 Framebuffer Object Queries, §6.1.14 Renderbuffer Object Queries, §6.1.15 Internal Format Queries, Tables 6.14 and 6.15 (initial state)
ES 3.0 §2.1.6.2 Conversion from Floating-Point to Normalized Fixed-Point (equation 2.3)
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.5.4 Default Precision Qualifiers, §7.1 gl_VertexID, §7.2 gl_FragCoord, §8.8 Texture Lookup Functions (texture, texelFetch)

api.glGenFramebuffers: ten scene framebuffers plus scratch ones; a generated name is not a framebuffer object (glIsFramebuffer FALSE) until bound
api.glBindFramebuffer: FRAMEBUFFER binds both targets, DRAW/READ_FRAMEBUFFER separately (all three binding queries); every scene is rendered through it and read back through it
api.glIsFramebuffer: FALSE for a fresh name and for 0, TRUE after the first bind, FALSE after delete
api.glDeleteFramebuffers: deleting the bound framebuffer reverts DRAW and READ bindings to 0; deleting the name 0 is silently ignored
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: COMPLETE for every scene framebuffer and the default one; MISSING_ATTACHMENT, INCOMPLETE_ATTACHMENT (zero-size / color format at depth point / depth format at color point / RGB9_E5 texture), UNSUPPORTED (separate depth and stencil images), INCOMPLETE_MULTISAMPLE; different attachment sizes stay COMPLETE
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: RGBA8 texture (level 0 and mip level 2) as COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 and a DEPTH_COMPONENT24 texture as DEPTH_ATTACHMENT: rendered pixels read back and sampled; INVALID_OPERATION for the default framebuffer and for a cube-map face target of a 2D texture
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: color, depth, stencil and DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT renderbuffers: depth- and stencil-tested draws only match the CPU model when attached; INVALID_OPERATION for the default framebuffer and for a non-renderbuffer name; renderbuffer 0 detaches
api.glGetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv: OBJECT_TYPE (TEXTURE / RENDERBUFFER / NONE), OBJECT_NAME, TEXTURE_LEVEL (0 and 2), TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP_FACE, RED..ALPHA/DEPTH/STENCIL_SIZE, COMPONENT_TYPE, COLOR_ENCODING, DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT shared object; INVALID_OPERATION for RED_SIZE of an empty point and COMPONENT_TYPE of DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT
api.glGenRenderbuffers: seven scene renderbuffers; a generated name is not a renderbuffer until bound
api.glBindRenderbuffer: RENDERBUFFER_BINDING reads back; deleting the bound renderbuffer reverts it to 0
api.glIsRenderbuffer: FALSE before the first bind, TRUE after, FALSE after delete
api.glDeleteRenderbuffers: deleting an attached renderbuffer detaches it from the bound framebuffer
api.glRenderbufferStorage: RGBA8, RGBA4, RGB5_A1, RGB565, RGB8, DEPTH_COMPONENT16/24, STENCIL_INDEX8, DEPTH24_STENCIL8: width, height, internal format and component sizes read back; width > MAX_RENDERBUFFER_SIZE -> INVALID_VALUE; changing storage changes completeness
api.glRenderbufferStorageMultisample: RENDERBUFFER_SAMPLES >= requested; a multisampled renderbuffer next to a single-sampled one -> INCOMPLETE_MULTISAMPLE; samples above the format's maximum -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glGetRenderbufferParameteriv: WIDTH, HEIGHT, INTERNAL_FORMAT, RED..STENCIL_SIZE, SAMPLES of seven sized formats and the initial state of a new renderbuffer (0x0, RGBA4, sizes 0; strict, ANGLE XFAIL for the sizes); INVALID_OPERATION with renderbuffer 0 bound
api.glGetInternalformativ: SAMPLES for RGBA8 renderbuffers: the largest count is >= MAX_SAMPLES and one more than it is rejected by glRenderbufferStorageMultisample
api.glGenTextures: color targets, a mip chain, a depth texture and scratch textures
api.glBindTexture: texture and mip-level attachments and their sampling in the second pass
api.glDeleteTextures: deleting an attached texture detaches it from the bound framebuffer
api.glTexImage2D: NULL-data storage for RGBA8, a 7-level chain, DEPTH_COMPONENT24 (DEPTH_COMPONENT/UNSIGNED_INT) and RGB9_E5 (not color-renderable); respecifying an attached texture changes completeness
api.glActiveTexture: unit 0 carries the texture sampled by the second pass
api.glBlitFramebuffer: 1:1 NEAREST copy of a color renderbuffer to the default framebuffer, cells equal the renderbuffer exactly; an incomplete READ framebuffer -> INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION
api.glReadPixels: RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE readback of every framebuffer object (compared with the CPU models) and of the default framebuffer cells; INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION on an incomplete framebuffer
api.glClear: COLOR/DEPTH/STENCIL of each scene; INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION on an incomplete framebuffer; a rejected clear leaves the attached texture unchanged
api.glClearColor: background color of every scene and of the default framebuffer, seen in the compared pixels
api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST and STENCIL_TEST: tested draws match the CPU depth/stencil pipeline
api.glDisable: DEPTH_TEST and STENCIL_TEST: the control cells differ from the tested ones exactly as the CPU model says
api.glDepthFunc: LESS: the later far quad does not overwrite the nearer one
api.glStencilFunc: ALWAYS/EQUAL with reference values 0..3: stencil values are made visible as colored bands
api.glStencilOp: REPLACE, INCR and depth-fail INCR counters verified through the visible bands
api.glColorMask: stencil-only writes (color masked off) leave the color unchanged
api.glViewport: target-sized viewports (64x64, 16x16 for mip level 2) and per-cell viewports
api.glGetUniformLocation: u_rect, u_z, u_color, u_size, u_tex, u_lod, u_lod_size, u_invert, u_gray located; their effect is visible in the pixels
api.glUniform1f: u_z, u_size, u_lod_size, u_invert, u_gray observed in the rendered images
api.glUniform1i: sampler unit (0) and u_lod (-1 = texture(), 2 = texelFetch of level 2)
api.glUniform4f: u_rect places the rectangles, u_color is their color; verified by pixel position and value
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLE_STRIP, 4 vertices from gl_VertexID; INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION on an incomplete framebuffer
api.glGetIntegerv: FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING, DRAW_/READ_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING, RENDERBUFFER_BINDING after bind / delete; MAX_RENDERBUFFER_SIZE and MAX_SAMPLES used for the boundary error cases

visual_review.notes: Viewed at 800x800 (llvmpipe, 4x3 cells, every 64x64 target shown 3x) and 640x400 (4x3 cells of 160x133, targets 2x). Row 1: gradient with checkerboard, its negative, the 16x16 level-2 pattern in 4m-pixel blocks, the stencil ring scene; row 2: D16 and D24 depth scenes, the depth-off control (red over green, blue stripe across), the solid red stencil-off control; row 3: DEPTH24_STENCIL8 (occlusion above, cyan/magenta/yellow stencil bands below), the depth-texture color cell, the depth texture as gray. Each target is centred in its cell with a gutter; no bleed between cells.
